retry.retryEvent: emit the existing retryable error envelope without end; record retryOrdinal/delayMs/errorCode only in private runtime audit data

cancellation.winnerRule: the first durable terminal transition under the job lock wins
cancellation.publishRule: publish rechecks the durable job state and resolvedRevision while holding the job lock; a durable cancellation before this check prevents publication, while a completed durable publish makes later cancellation JOB_NOT_CANCELLABLE
cancellation.partialArtifactRule: completed and failed observation artifacts remain auditable; no partial profile becomes ready

workerRecovery.expiryRule: an expired running lease is reclaimed by one worker under the job lock
workerRecovery.uncertainExternalCallRule: a lease expiry after durable lease acquisition is treated as one consumed attempt; recovery may retry only under retryEligibility
workerRecovery.preLeaseCrashRule: a crash before durable lease acquisition may be reclaimed without consuming an attempt
workerRecovery.staleWorkerRule: completion with a non-current lease token is rejected without publication
workerRecovery.recoveryEvent: record recovery only in private runtime audit data; external SSE emits no worker identifier or new warning code

sseReplay.eventIdRule: strictly increasing positive per-job IDs; never reused
sseReplay.lastEventIdRule: replay only events with eventId greater than Last-Event-ID
sseReplay.expiredRetentionRule: emit a current stage snapshot and require GET job retrieval for final artifacts
sseReplay.terminalRule: exactly one end event follows final result or error; no event is legal after end

publication.atomicityBoundary: single process lock plus atomic same-directory replacement for JSON artifacts
publication.recoveryRule: startup reconciliation treats a valid pointer and profile artifact for the same job/request as a completed publication, appends only missing terminal events, and never republishes a different profile
publication.staleRule: a changed resolvedRevision atomically records superseded and leaves the prior completed pointer unchanged
